name: Priority Setting Ad Hoc Committee Liaison Meeting Agenda
minutes_text:
CITY OF BEVERLY HILLS
  455 North Rexford Drive
  Beverly Hills, CA 90210
  Video Teleconference
  Beverly Hills City Council Liaison / Priority Setting Ad Hoc Committee Meeting

  SPECIAL MEETING HIGHLIGHTS

  Wednesday, April 30, 2025
  2:30 PM

MEETING CALLED TO ORDER
Date / Time:  April 30, 2025 / 2:30 PM
IN ATTENDANCE:  Mayor Sharona Nazarian, Councilmember Craig Corman, City Manager
  Nancy Hunt-Coffey

  1) Public Comment:
  None

  2) Review Draft Priorities for Fiscal Year 2025 - 2026:
  a. Global Comments:
  i. Staff will cut the percentages from the final document, as there was a lot of
  confusion around what units the percentages measured, as it varied from
  item to item.
  ii. The liaisons do want indicators to show the public that progress has been
  made on specific items.
  iii. Staff is looking for ways to incorporate planning the Commission priorities
  into the City priority planning process.
  1. This would include biannual Council Liaison check ins with the
  Commissions around June and December to update the Council on
  what progress the Commissions have made on their yearly
  workplan.
  iv. Both Liaison expressed the notion that for a “simplified” priorities document,
  it was rather complicated.
  v. The Mayor indicated that she would like for each work plan item to state if
  a Commission works on the item, and if so, which Commission.
  vi. The Liaisons would also like for the cut items to be presented as their own
  list at the Council Meeting to implement the draft priorities.
  b. SP1:
  i. WP1.2.3: Mayor Nazarian inquired about the possibility of using ALPR’s to
  read a vehicle’s VIN number.
  ii. WP1.2.4 - MS 1: Force Metrics is a data miner used by the Police
  Department to analyze online activity for potential threats to the City, which
  includes sending real time alerts to PD.
  iii. WP1.2.7 MS 1: ITAM will track City computers and make sure that all
  systems are up to date to prevent security vulnerabilities.
 Highlights for April 30, 2025
Priority Setting Ad Hoc Committee

  iv. WP1.2.8: This item mostly concerns replacing outdated computers, and it
  is already budgeted for.
  v. WP1.2.8: The Mayor would like to create an Ad Hoc to review changes and
  improvements to the Police Department in a holistic manner.
  vi. WP1.4.2: The Liaisons would like this item to include the difference
  between how public and private properties are affected by the VHFHSZ
  changes.
  c. SP2:
  i. WP2.2.3: The wording for this item will be changed, since Staff only plans
  on doing the prework for implementing this item, as the full implementation
  of this item is planned for FY 2026 – 2027.
  ii. WP2.2.4: This item, particularly concerning using AI for staff reports, is
  currently in a trial stage.
  iii. WP2.2.4: The Mayor inquired about the possibility of using AI to review
  construction permit applications.
  iv. WP2.2.5 - MS 3: This item will be cut, as it concerns the rollout of
  WaterSmart, which had already been completed in FY 2024 - 2025.
  v. WP2.2.7 - MS 1: How the City will get public feedback is still up in the air,
  as this was previously done by the Sunshine Task Force, but that
  Committee no longer exists.
  d. SP3:
  i. WP3.1.6: Councilmember Corman pointed out that these appraisals are
  not expensive and that the City does not have much art worthy of appraisal
  anyway.
  ii. WP3.1.8: the Mayor would like for this item to include Mayoral initiatives.
  e. SP4:
  i. WP4.2.1: The City will be moving towards implementing a cost neutral fee
  system over the course of the next three years.
  ii. WP4.2.2 - MS 2: The Mayor would like this item to clarify that this would be
  done via integration with existing city events.
  f. SP5:
  i. WP5.1.2: This is a necessary health and safety item.
  ii. WP5.1.5: The Liaisons would like for this item to be implemented this year,
  even if it will not be completed by the end of the fiscal year.
  iii. WP5.1.8: The Mayor would like to create an Ad Hoc to review this item
  (mentioned in a comment on WP1.2.8).
  iv. WP5.1.12: The mayor would like for a detailed plan to be made for this
  item.
  v. WP5.1.14: The Liaisons would like for staff to check to see if this is a priority
  or a Wishlist item.
  1. There is a possibility that this item relates to state laws around
  gender neutral bathrooms, in which case it would be a necessary
  item.
  vi. WP5.1.15: The Liaisons would like for staff to check to see if this is a priority
  or a Wishlist item from the Clerk’s office, especially since they recently
  expanded.
  vii. WP5.2.4: Both Liaisons want this item removed due to cost, and further
  noted that only Councilmember Mirisch was in favor of restoring this item
  to the priority list at the City Council meeting concerning this item.
  viii. WP5.3.3: The Mayor would like to investigate the possibility of using AI for
  certain applications that are covered by this item.
 Highlights for April 30, 2025
Priority Setting Ad Hoc Committee

  g. SP6:
  i. WP6.1.1 - MS 1: The Liaisons would like for the City to make very clear
  that this site is currently being used by Metro and to meticulously document
  any delays to the cessation of construction by Metro for future discussions
  concerning the City’s housing element.
  ii. WP6.1.3: The Liaisons stated that this is a priority item to complete this
  fiscal year.
  iii. WP6.2.1: The liaisons would like for staff to review the specific wording of
  this item in the housing element, as if it is not required, the City is not in the
  budgetary situation to be able to implement this item.
  iv. WP6.2.3: Both Liaisons would like for this item to be cut due to the City’s
  budget deficit.
  1. This was based on a COVID era program that had a $1 million
  budget and did not expend even half of that, so the council at the
  time indicated their willingness to looking at permanently
  implementing a variation of the program.
  v. WP6.3.1: The Liaisons wanted to clarify that these objective design
  standards will be in line with state law.
  h. SP7:
  i. G7.2: The Mayor would like to add the workplan item “Review Electrical
  Grid Resilience” to this section.
  ii. WP7.2.3: The Mayor cautioned about rushing into completing this item
  without ensuring electrical grid compliance.
  i. Commission Priorities:
  i. The Council would use the sample priority setting grid in the Staff Report
  to review specific Commission priorities.
  j. City Events:
  i. The Mayor would like to have a unified event list with budgets presented to
  the City Council at some point in the future.
  ii. The City will create a zero base event list with the RDC Liaison within the
  next 6 months.

  3) Adjournment:
  Date / Time: April 30, 2025 / 3:51 PM
